_comment: Citations for the five Chapter Approved 2025-26 primary missions newly modelled behind SWEG_PRIMARY_DECK_FULL (default-off): Linchpin, Burden of Trust, Unexploded Ordnance, Hidden Supplies, Supply Drop. The other five cards (Take and Hold, Terraform, Purge the Foe, Scorched Earth, The Ritual) were already modelled and are cited in data/rule_citations.d/core_primary_vp_cap.json. All quoted_text below is verbatim, cross-checked against the raw Wahapedia page HTML (not just the rendered summary) on 2026-07-08. Wahapedia source: https://wahapedia.ru/wh40k10ed/the-rules/chapter-approved-2025-26/

simulator.primary_linchpin.quoted_text: If the player whose turn it is does not control the objective marker in their deployment zone, they score 3VP for each objective marker they control. OR If the player whose turn it is controls the objective marker in their deployment zone, they score 3VP for controlling that objective marker, and 5VP for each other objective marker they control (up to 15VP per turn).
simulator.primary_linchpin.trigger: SECOND BATTLE ROUND ONWARDS. End of the Command phase (or the end of your turn if it is the fifth battle round and you are going second).
simulator.primary_linchpin.effect: SWEG_PRIMARY_DECK_FULL (Battle._score_objectives, mission == 'linchpin'). a_home_ctrl / b_home_ctrl (computed in the per-objective loop via _obj_in_own_dz) record whether the side controls the single objective marker in its own deployment zone. If so: min(3 + 5 * (other controlled markers), 15). If not (including the common case on 3 of the 5 rotation maps where NO objective ever sits in a deployment zone, so the condition is vacuously true every game): 3VP per controlled marker, uncapped per the verbatim text (naturally bounded to 15 anyway since no stock map carries more than 5 objectives). No approximation beyond the existing point-objective model shared with every other mission.

simulator.primary_burden_of_trust.rule_name: Burden of Trust primary mission scoring (Chapter Approved 2025-26)
simulator.primary_burden_of_trust.quoted_text: At the end of the Command phase, for each objective marker the player whose turn it is controls, they can select one unit from their army (excluding AIRCRAFT) within range of that objective marker to guard it until the start of their next turn. ... The player whose turn it is scores 4VP for each objective marker they control that is not within their deployment zone. ... The opponent of the player whose turn it is scores 2VP for each of their units (excluding Battle-shocked units) that are within range of and guarding an objective marker they control.
simulator.primary_burden_of_trust.trigger: SECOND BATTLE ROUND ONWARDS. Hold clause: end of the Command phase (or end of turn, fifth-round-going-second exception). Guard-scoring clause: end of each player's turn, scored by the player who is NOT currently active, for their own guarding units.
simulator.primary_burden_of_trust.effect: SWEG_PRIMARY_DECK_FULL (Battle._score_objectives, mission == 'burden_of_trust'). Only the hold clause is modelled: 4VP per objective controlled outside the controller's own deployment zone (a_controls_nondz / b_controls_nondz from the per-objective loop), with NO cap applied — verified verbatim, this is the only CA-2025-26 primary hold clause without a stated per-round ceiling. PARTIAL, disclosed: the guard/2VP clause requires true per-player-turn granularity (nominate a guard at one player's Command phase, score it at the OTHER player's end of turn) that the round-batched scorer does not have, and is NOT modelled — the same documented-gap pattern already used for The Ritual's un-modelled Action (data/rule_citations.d/core_primary_vp_cap.json, simulator.primary_the_ritual).

simulator.primary_unexploded_ordnance.rule_name: Unexploded Ordnance primary mission scoring (Chapter Approved 2025-26)
simulator.primary_unexploded_ordnance.quoted_text: Start of the Battle: Each objective marker within No Man's Land becomes a Hazard objective marker. ... You can move each of those Hazard objective markers up to 6". ... The player whose turn it is scores VP as follows: 8VP for each Hazard objective marker that is wholly within their opponent's deployment zone. 5VP for each other Hazard objective marker that is wholly within 6" of their opponent's deployment zone. 2VP for each other Hazard objective marker that is wholly within 12" of their opponent's deployment zone.
simulator.primary_unexploded_ordnance.trigger: Start of the Battle (Hazard designation, applies to every objective already in No Man's Land — no new markers added). SECOND BATTLE ROUND ONWARDS, end of each player's turn, for the VP bands.
simulator.primary_unexploded_ordnance.effect: SWEG_PRIMARY_DECK_FULL (Battle._score_objectives, mission == 'unexploded_ordnance'). Every No Man's Land objective is treated as a Hazard marker (no separate flag needed — _obj_in_nml already identifies them). VP banded by distance from the marker's FIXED position to the opponent's deployment-zone edge: <=6" scores 5VP, <=12" scores 2VP (a_uo_vp / b_uo_vp accumulated in the per-objective loop). PARTIAL, disclosed: the Move Hazard Action (repositioning a controlled Hazard marker up to 6" per turn) is NOT modelled, so the 8VP 'wholly within opponent's deployment zone' band is mathematically unreachable here — a No Man's Land marker's fixed position is by construction never inside either deployment zone (_obj_in_nml requires deployment_width < y < height - deployment_width). This is an honest under-count versus the real card, the same fixed-marker-position limitation as The Ritual's un-modelled Action.

simulator.primary_hidden_supplies.rule_name: Hidden Supplies primary mission scoring (Chapter Approved 2025-26)
simulator.primary_hidden_supplies.quoted_text: In the Place Objective Markers step, players must set up one additional objective marker in No Man's Land. ... The player whose turn it is scores VP as follows (these are cumulative): 5VP If they control one objective marker not within their deployment zone. 5VP If they control two objective markers not within their deployment zone. 5VP if they control more objective markers than their opponent controls.
simulator.primary_hidden_supplies.trigger: Place Objective Markers step (extra marker setup). SECOND BATTLE ROUND ONWARDS, end of the Command phase (or end of turn, fifth-round-going-second exception), for the cumulative VP bullets.
simulator.primary_hidden_supplies.effect: SWEG_PRIMARY_DECK_FULL (Battle._score_objectives, mission == 'hidden_supplies'). Cumulative: 5VP if a_controls_nondz >= 1, +5VP if >= 2, +5VP if a_controls > b_controls (the third bullet is unqualified in the source text, unlike the first two, so — matching Purge the Foe's identically-unqualified 'more objective markers than their opponent controls' clause, simulator.primary_purge_the_foe — it reads off the ALL-objectives control counts, not the not-in-own-deployment-zone subset). PARTIAL, disclosed: the setup step (an additional objective marker in No Man's Land, placed after repositioning the centre marker toward a corner) is NOT modelled — the simulator's per-map objective set is fixed at map-build time, so this scores against the EXISTING marker set only, the same fixed-objective-set limitation as The Ritual's un-modelled Action.

simulator.primary_supply_drop.rule_name: Supply Drop primary mission scoring (Chapter Approved 2025-26)
simulator.primary_supply_drop.quoted_text: Start of the Battle: Players randomly select two different objective markers within No Man's Land that are not in the centre of the battlefield; the first selected is the Alpha objective, the second selected is the Omega objective. Start of the Fourth Battle Round: The Alpha objective is removed from the battlefield. Start of the Fifth Battle Round: The Omega objective is removed from the battlefield. ... The player whose turn it is scores the following VP for each objective marker in No Man's Land that they control, depending on the current battle round: 5VP in the second and third battle rounds. 8VP in the fourth battle round. 15VP in the fifth battle round.
simulator.primary_supply_drop.trigger: Start of the Battle (Alpha/Omega designation). Start of battle round 4 (Alpha removed) and round 5 (Omega removed). SECOND BATTLE ROUND ONWARDS, end of the Command phase (or end of turn, fifth-round-going-second exception), for the escalating per-marker VP.
simulator.primary_supply_drop.effect: SWEG_PRIMARY_DECK_FULL (Battle._score_objectives, mission == 'supply_drop'; Battle._assign_supply_drop_targets / _resolve_supply_drop_removals, gated SWEG_SUPPLY_DROP). Scoring is over ALL remaining (non-razed) No Man's Land markers at the round's escalating per-marker rate (5/8/15VP), matching the verbatim 'for each objective marker in No Man's Land that they control' wording — Alpha/Omega only decide which TWO markers get permanently razed (added to the existing _razed_objectives bucket Scorched Earth's Burn uses) at the start of rounds 4 and 5, shrinking the pool as the per-marker value rises. No cap applied — verified verbatim, no '(up to NVP per turn)' phrase appears on this card. PARTIAL, disclosed: the real Alpha/Omega pick is RANDOM; _assign_supply_drop_targets picks the first two non-centre No Man's Land markers in map-definition order instead, so drawing this mission never consumes an extra draw from the battle's seeded random stream (which would otherwise perturb every subsequent random decision in that same game — unit placement jitter, hit/wound rolls — making even the gate-OFF path only conditionally byte-identical).
